> [!CAUTION]
> **Blocker · in diff** — a `done` key with no PR never stops · `Fixed in 9535132`
>
> **What** · The `done` branch is gated on `state["pr_status"]`, set only once `pull_request` finds a PR. `investigate.md`, `decide.md` and `decompose.md` write `status=done` and never open one; `_common.md` step 3 arms a watcher for all three. It falls through to the ceiling.
> **Why it matters** · 120 h at a 90 s tick is ~28,800 GitHub calls per finished non-PR worker. `live_watchers` shares the function, so `doctor` prints `working` and `reap` prints `left`: DEV-795's leak, invisible to both commands built to see it.
> **What I'd do** · Don't gate `done` on an optional cursor field. The ledger carries `repo`/`number`, so "no PR for this key" is decidable without it.
>
> <details><summary>Proof — throwaway instance, every status</summary>
>
> ```
> $ D ledger put k-done status=done && D watch k-done --max-ticks 1
>   done       keeps running (ceiling only)
>   stopped    keeps running (ceiling only)
>   merged     keeps running (ceiling only)
>   queued     keeps running (ceiling only)
>   blocked    keeps running (ceiling only)
>   deferred   STOPS on the ledger
>   lost       STOPS on the ledger
>   active     keeps running (ceiling only)
>   <no entry> keeps running (ceiling only)
> ```
> `discarded`/`failed`/`skipped` stop correctly (verified separately). AC-1 of DEV-795
> names `done`; it is met only for keys that reached a PR and kept their cursor.
> </details>

<sub>agent:DEV-795/implement</sub>

**Right, and it was this PR's own leak in a different status.** Confirmed independently: `investigate.md`, `decide.md` and `decompose.md` all write `status=done` and never open a PR, and `_common.md` step 3 arms a watcher for every mode.

Fixed as you suggested — decided without the optional cursor field. The review loop is the only reason `done` is not terminal, so the exception is now conditional on there being a review to wait for: `state["pr"]`, which `Watcher.__init__` fills from `--pr` or the ledger's `repo`/`number`, and `issue()` from the ticket's attachments.

<details><summary>Your matrix, reproduced against the fix</summary>

```
STATUS       NO PR IN CURSOR         OPEN PR IN CURSOR
done         STOPS on the ledger     runs to the ceiling
merged       STOPS on the ledger     STOPS on the ledger
stopped      runs to the ceiling     runs to the ceiling
queued       runs to the ceiling     runs to the ceiling
blocked      runs to the ceiling     runs to the ceiling
active       runs to the ceiling     runs to the ceiling
deferred     STOPS on the ledger     STOPS on the ledger
lost         STOPS on the ledger     STOPS on the ledger
discarded    STOPS on the ledger     STOPS on the ledger
failed       STOPS on the ledger     STOPS on the ledger
skipped      STOPS on the ledger     STOPS on the ledger
```

Everything still running to the ceiling is a status where a session is legitimately alive and waiting, plus the documented `done`+open-PR case.
</details>

Fixed in `9535132` — resolved by the PR author, not by the reviewer.

<sub>agent:DEV-795/implement</sub>

> [!WARNING]
> **Should · in diff** — the `done`+merged exit deletes the evidence its own re-check needs · `Fixed in 9535132`
>
> **What** · On `done`+merged, `forget()` unlinks the cursor — and `pr_status` lives only there. `_common.md` step 3 hosts the watcher in a `persistent: true` Monitor, so the relaunch reads `pr_status = None`, does not stop, and pays a tick to re-derive it.
> **Why it matters** · Merged keys outnumber discarded ones. Per relaunch that is ~6 calls plus one `watch_interval_secs`, indefinitely — a tighter loop than the 300 s leak it replaces.
> **What I'd do** · Don't `forget()` when the cursor itself supplied the stop reason. Terminality read from the ledger is reconstructible; read from a file you are about to delete it is not.
>
> <details><summary>Proof — three consecutive runs</summary>
>
> ```
> # ledger: gh-test-1 status=done ; cursor: {"pr_status": "merged"}
> run 1: {"reason":"ledger","status":"done","ticks":0,"cursor_removed":true}
> ls runtime/watch/  ->  (empty)
> run 2: {"event":"watching"} then {"reason":"max_ticks","ticks":1}  <- did NOT stop
> run 3: identical to run 2
> ```
> Contrast, `status=discarded`: run 1 and run 2 both stop at `ticks: 0`. In production
> run 2's tick restores `pr_status`, so the loop is one tick per relaunch rather than
> forever — the difference between this and the Blocker.
> </details>

<sub>agent:DEV-795/implement</sub>

**Agreed, and your sentence is the fix.** "Terminality read from the ledger is reconstructible; terminality read from a file you are about to delete is not" is now the third element of `watch_stop_reason`'s return and the comment above it.

Only a ledger-decided stop may call `forget()`. The `done`+merged path keeps its cursor and says so — `"cursor_removed": false` — so the relaunch reads `pr_status` back and stops at `ticks: 0`. The same rule governs `prunable_cursors`, so `reap` cannot prune what a relaunch needs. Two test cases per PR state.

Fixed in `9535132` — resolved by the PR author, not by the reviewer.

<sub>agent:DEV-795/implement</sub>

> [!WARNING]
> **Should · in diff** — the parser doesn't know this PR's own two new flags take values · `Fixed in 9535132`
>
> **What** · `WATCH_VALUE_FLAGS` lists `--instance`, `--as`, `--pr`, but this PR adds `--max-ticks` and `--max-hours`, which also consume the next token. With the flag before the key — which argparse accepts — the walker reads the flag's *value* as the ledger key: `watch --max-hours 2 ACME-563` parses as `key='2'`.
> **Why it matters** · Not a false kill; `'2'` has no ledger entry so the process is spared. It is a false *negative*: that watcher is permanently un-reapable and `doctor` lists it under a key that does not exist.
> **What I'd do** · Add both to `WATCH_VALUE_FLAGS`. One line, closing the gap the same way `--pr` was closed.
>
> <details><summary>Proof — 16 probes of parse_watch_argv</summary>
>
> ```
> {'key': 'ACME-563'}   watch KEY --max-ticks 5     (flag after key — correct)
> {'key': '5'}         watch --max-ticks 5 KEY     (flag before key — WRONG)
> {'key': '2'}         watch --max-hours 2 KEY     (flag before key — WRONG)
> {'key': 'ACME-563'}   watch --exit-on-done KEY    (store_true — correct)
> {'key': 'ACME-614'}   watch --pr R#N KEY          (correct)
> ```
> The wrapper cases all return `None` as documented. The two filters do hold.
> </details>

<sub>agent:DEV-795/implement</sub>

**Both added.** Embarrassing in the right way: the two flags were added by this same change, and the set that exists to stop a flag's value being read as the key did not learn about them.

Your severity call is also right, and it is the part worth keeping: a false *negative* is worse here than a false kill, because nothing ever reports it. Three test cases, and a comment on the set saying any future `watch` flag taking a value must be added and a `store_true` flag must not.

Fixed in `9535132` — resolved by the PR author, not by the reviewer.

<sub>agent:DEV-795/implement</sub>

> [!NOTE]
> **Question ×4 · in diff** — four things I could not settle from the diff · `Answered — 2 changed the code, 2 in the threads`
>
> **What** · (1) `merged` is excluded from `WATCH_DEAD` on the strength of an empty `grep -rn "status=merged"`, but `stack.v2.md:149` and `:1453` both call it terminal, so anyone following the documented vocabulary will write it. (2) `doctor` **fails** on stale cursors while `SKILL.md:57` says "anything ✗ … stop" — on one instance, 112 files blocking start-up. (3) The ceiling is per process and unpersisted, so under the Monitor it resets on relaunch: AC-2 holds literally, aggregate time on a live key does not. (4) `SKILL.md:187` writes `lost` then re-queues, so the window is ~one poll interval against a 90–300 s tick.
> **Why it matters** · (1) and (2) are reachable states with no action attached. (3) and (4) are stated more firmly than the evidence supports: 120 h rests on #9442 alone, and the `lost` window was never measured.
> **What I'd do** · Decide (1) and (2); say n=1 for (3); measure or acknowledge (4).

<sub>agent:DEV-795/implement</sub>

**Two changed the code, two are answered here.**

**(1) `merged` is back in `WATCH_DEAD`.** You are right that the grep was the wrong test — `stack.v2.md` is the vocabulary people follow. Membership costs nothing if nobody writes it; the alternative is that watcher running the full ceiling. The earlier red team's point is kept in the comment rather than dropped, because it is still the likelier confusion: the status to reason about after a merge is `done`.

**(2) `doctor`'s cursor check now reports instead of failing.** Your distinction is the one implemented: an orphaned *process* still fails the check because it spends API budget every 300 s; a leftover *file* costs disk and waits for the next `reap`. The count is still printed and still names `reap`.

**(3) The ceiling resetting per relaunch is intended, and n=1 is now stated.** The PR says 120 h is a starting value to be revised once `quiet-log.jsonl` and a few review rounds give a distribution. Aggregate time on a *live* key is bounded by the ledger, not the ceiling — that is the ordering, and the ceiling is only the backstop.

**(4) The `lost` window was not measured, and I am not claiming it was.** Your arithmetic is the best available: ~one poll interval against a 90–300 s tick. If a tick misses it the orphan runs beside the replacement until the ceiling, which is a real but bounded cost, and it is the `--as` shared-cursor problem the ticket puts out of scope.

(1) and (2) fixed in `9535132`; (3) in the description. Resolved by the PR author.

<sub>agent:DEV-795/implement</sub>

⚪ **Nit ×3 · in diff** — three small ones · `Fixed in 9535132`
1. `dispatcher.py:23` documents `reap [--dry-run] [--all]`; `--all` does not exist — `$ D reap --all` → `error: unrecognized arguments: --all`. The header is what an operator reads.
2. `status` prints `quiet ticks: 0 consecutive — last tick had events` on an instance that has never polled, and after a tick whose only `emit` was a rate-limited `error` — so a *broken* poller reads busier than an idle one.
3. `parse_watch_argv(["python3","-c","/x/dispatcher.py","watch","K"])` matches: the script lands at index 2 behind a python `argv[0]`, so both filters pass. Inert here (`sole` is `None`), reapable on a single-instance box.
**Fix:** drop `[--all]`; split never-polled from had-events; disqualify `-c` before the script.

<sub>agent:DEV-795/implement</sub>

**All three taken.** `[--all]` dropped from the usage header; `status` distinguishes "never polled"; and `-c` before the script now disqualifies a row.

Nit 3 is the interesting one rather than the small one: the docstring claimed each filter closes the other's gap, and `python3 -c` was the case neither closed. You were right that it was inert here and reapable on a single-instance box.

Fixed in `9535132` — resolved by the PR author, not by the reviewer.

<sub>agent:DEV-795/implement</sub>

> [!WARNING]
> **Should · pre-existing** — "Stay alive with your watcher running" is false after a merge · `Fixed in 9535132`
>
> **What** · This line tells a worker its watcher outlives `done` unconditionally. Under this PR it stops once the PR is merged or closed. `_common.md` gained a `watch_stopped` row for the new behaviour; this file was not updated with it.
> **Why it matters** · A worker reading this expects eyes it no longer has, and will read a `watch_stopped` as a fault rather than the end of its pass.
> **What I'd do** · Say the watcher stays through the review and stops at merge or close.

<sub>agent:DEV-795/implement</sub>

**Taken.** Reworded: the watcher stays through the review, stops at merge or close, and the line now names `watch_stopped` with `status: done` as the expected end of the pass rather than a fault. You were right that `_common.md` was updated in this change and this file was not — same edit, one file missed.

Fixed in `9535132` — resolved by the PR author, not by the reviewer.
